text:
alex.k: hitting a weird 403 when trying to run the sample app locally after setting up the dev proxy. anyone seen this?
megan.d: post the error and the exact env vars you set?
alex.k: sure — i set HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY to our corp proxy, exported REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID, then: 
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
* HTTP/2 403
* {"error":"org_billing_missing: workspace requires billing setup"}
```
alex.k: odd because the workspace appears under my org in the console and shows as "trial"
samir: that error is thrown from the auth layer if the token is valid but the workspace doesn't have billing enabled. could be a mismatch between workspace id and token scope. are you using a service key or a personal key?
alex.k: personal key from my profile page. i just invited an account email to the workspace yesterday though.
megan.d: if you invited the email, they might not have accepted, or the workspace id you exported is for the org's sandbox workspace (no billing). check the workspace slug in the console UI and confirm the id matches.
alex.k: confirmed — the id matches. i accepted the invite weeks ago.
megan.d: another possibility: proxy is rewriting headers and dropping the org header we add for workspace lookups. can you run with no proxy (temporarily) or curl --noproxy localhost?
alex.k: i tried bypassing proxy and still see the same 403. logs from SDK: 
"status:403, code:org_billing_missing, msg: Workspace requires billing info to enable hosted inference. See https://redwood.ai/docs/onboarding#billing"
megan.d: okay that narrows it to billing gate. @devex-bot can we confirm workspace billing state for alex.k's workspace id  ws_abc123?
devex-bot: workspace ws_abc123: status=trial, billing_info=missing, invited_admins=[alex.k] (unpaid trial) — contact billing to convert to paid or add a credit card. Docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/onboarding#billing
samir: quick workaround for local dev: generate a temporary dedicated dev token from your org's sandbox if you have a dev plan, or use the self-hosted Private deployment endpoint if available. otherwise add billing info to the workspace.
alex.k: ugh we don't want to add org card for a dev test. is there a programmatic bypass?
megan.d: not for hosted API; the billing gate is enforced server-side. we could create a new personal workspace (free dev workspace) under your user account that doesn't require org billing — but that's a different workspace id.
alex.k: i tried creating a new personal workspace but the SDK still picks up REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID from env and i keep hitting the old one.
megan.d: unset REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID locally or set REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID=<new_ws_id>. also check cached credentials in ~/.redwood/credentials.json — SDK reads both env and local cache.
alex.k: found the cached creds, cleared them, retried without proxy and it works! first call succeeded 
* response: {"id":"gen_01","status":"ok","text":"hello"}
alex.k: so two things: (1) billing gate message is accurate — not a proxy header issue, and (2) cached workspace id made debugging confusing.
samir: filed a tiny DX follow-up: add clearer error guidance in the SDK error object — include a direct link to console billing page and a machine-readable subcode for 'billing_required'. also add a note in the quickstart that cached creds can override env vars.
megan.d: :+1: can you open a short PR to docs and an issue for the SDK change? label devex-onboarding.
alex.k: filing now. thanks all!
megan.d: glad it's resolved. leaving a checklist here for devs who hit this: 
- confirm which workspace id the SDK is using (env vs cache)
- bypass proxy to rule out header loss
- check devex-bot workspace billing state
- create personal dev workspace if you don't want to add org billing

samir: adding ticket: RED-DEVEX-452 — SDK should return structured error: { code: "billing_required", docs_url: "https://redwood.ai/docs/onboarding#billing" }
alex.k: thanks — saved me a bunch of time. :coffee:
